{
  "skills": [
    {
      "skill_id": "polar_halogen_hydration_balance",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "hetero_rich_polar_favored",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_high"},
          "weight": 0.7,
          "rationale": "Multiple N/O sites donate and accept water hydrogen bonds, the leading favorable term in hydration free energy."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "halogen_rich_penalized",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_high"},
          "weight": -0.55,
          "rationale": "Halogen-rich surfaces are polarizable but weak hydrogen bonders, raising cavity-formation cost in water."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "nonpolar_bare_carbon_penalized",
          "conditions": {"hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_none"},
          "weight": -0.4,
          "rationale": "Hydrocarbon-only solutes hydrate poorly; the dominant cost is creating a cavity in water's hydrogen-bond network."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "polar_moderate_no_halogen_bonus",
          "conditions": {"halogen_bin": "halogen_none", "hetero_atom_bin": "hetero_mid"},
          "weight": 0.3,
          "rationale": "Moderate polarity without halogen quenching is the classic favorable hydration regime for small organic solutes."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.5,
      "prior_scale": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.35,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.1,
      "ucb_weight": 0.55,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.2,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.02,
      "confidence": 0.6,
      "hypothesis": "Hydration affinity is set by polar hydrogen-bonding capacity minus hydrophobic cavity cost, so heteroatom-rich and halogen-free solutes rank highest. Fails if the target score rewards burial of polar groups or halogen bonding."
    },
    {
      "skill_id": "aromatic_ring_hydrophobicity_penalty",
      "rules": [
        {
          "rule_id": "aromatic_high_penalized",
          "conditions": {"aromatic_bin": "aromatic_high"},
          "weight": -0.6,
          "rationale": "Highly aromatic scaffolds present flat nonpolar faces; desolvation of these faces dominates the hydration penalty."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "ring_token_high_penalized",
          "conditions": {"ring_token_bin": "ring_token_high"},
          "weight": -0.45,
          "rationale": "Rigid polycyclic topology is bulky and poorly matched to water's hydrogen-bond network, raising cavity work."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "acyclic_low_branch_favored",
          "conditions": {"branch_bin": "branch_none"},
          "weight": 0.3,
          "rationale": "Unbranched acyclic solutes pack compactly, minimizing exposed hydrophobic surface per unit of polar functionality."
        },
        {
          "rule_id": "counter_short_smiles_downweighted",
          "conditions": {"smiles_length_bin": "smiles_short"},
          "weight": 0.15,
          "rationale": "Counter-hypothesis: the ESOL size prior had only 0.22 confidence, so its short-SMILES bonus is heavily damped."
        }
      ],
      "ridge": 1.0,
      "prior_scale": 0.25,
      "semantic_mass_start": 0.3,
      "semantic_mass_end": 0.08,
      "ucb_weight": 0.6,
      "gp_beta_start": 2.0,
      "gp_beta_end": 1.0,
      "gp_xi": 0.01,
      "confidence": 0.45,
      "hypothesis": "Hydrophobic scaffold exposure, not molecular size, governs hydration ranking: aromatic and ring-rich topologies are penalized while acyclic low-branch solutes gain. Fails if polar functionalization outweighs scaffold shape."
    }
  ],
  "selected_skill_id": "polar_halogen_hydration_balance",
  "lesson": "Across the eight development seeds the polarity/hydrogen-bonding skill roughly doubled mean rank AUC versus the size-and-ring transfer (72.9 vs 54.3), with the size skill collapsing on some seeds; scaffold-shape rules were retained only as a lower-confidence complement. The evidence is directional, not causal, from a small seed set.",
  "revision_summary": "Retained the winning polar mechanism but hardened it: added an explicit hetero_none penalty and kept the halogen and halogen-free/moderate-polarity interactions, dropping the near-inert smiles_mid counter rule. The second skill replaces the source-heavy size transfer with a distinct hydrophobic-scaffold hypothesis that penalizes aromatic and ring-rich topology, and it downweights instead of honoring the weak 0.22-confidence short-SMILES prior. Both skills decay semantic mass so target-only GP evidence takes over late; the polar skill is frozen for deployment."
}
